topicDisplay: Christianity through a Study of the Gospel of Matthew

learningObjectives.title: The birth and early ministry of Jesus
The death and resurrection of Jesus

questions.q: The wise men (Magi) brought the infant Jesus three gifts. Which were they?
questions.explain: In Matthew 2 the Magi present gold, frankincense and myrrh to the young Jesus.

questions.q: Who appeared to Joseph in a dream and told him to take Mary as his wife?
questions.explain: An angel of the Lord reassured Joseph that Mary's child had been conceived through the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Matthew says Jesus would be called 'Emmanuel'. What does this name signify?
questions.explain: Matthew explains that Emmanuel means 'God with us', presenting Jesus as God's presence among people.

questions.q: Why did Joseph take Mary and Jesus to Egypt?
options: To escape Herod's plan to kill the child
To register for the Roman census
To find work as a carpenter
questions.explain: Warned in a dream, Joseph fled to Egypt to protect Jesus from Herod's massacre of the infants.

questions.q: Who baptised Jesus in the River Jordan?
questions.explain: John the Baptist baptised Jesus in the Jordan, after which the Spirit descended like a dove.

questions.q: At Jesus' baptism a voice from heaven declared him to be God's beloved Son. What was the significance of this?
options: It publicly affirmed Jesus' identity and God's approval
It appointed John as the Messiah
It marked the beginning of the Passover
questions.explain: The heavenly voice identified Jesus as God's Son, confirming his mission at the start of his ministry.

questions.q: When tempted to turn stones into bread, Jesus replied, 'Man shall not live by bread alone.' What does his response best demonstrate?
options: His reliance on God's word to resist temptation
questions.explain: Jesus answers each temptation by quoting scripture, showing dependence on God rather than on worldly needs.

questions.q: What name is given to the series of blessings that open the Sermon on the Mount?
questions.explain: The Beatitudes are the 'Blessed are...' sayings that begin the Sermon on the Mount in Matthew 5.

questions.q: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called...' Complete the beatitude.
questions.explain: Matthew 5 records, 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.'

questions.q: The Lord's Prayer is given by Jesus as part of which body of teaching?
questions.explain: Jesus teaches the Lord's Prayer within the Sermon on the Mount as a model of how to pray.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Sower, what does the seed represent?
questions.explain: Jesus explains the seed is the message of the kingdom, received differently depending on the 'soil' of the heart.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats, Jesus says that helping the hungry, sick and imprisoned is really doing what?
questions.explain: 'Whatever you did for one of the least of these... you did for me' links care for others to service of Christ.

questions.q: The feeding of the five thousand from five loaves and two fish primarily demonstrates what about Jesus?
options: His compassion and miraculous power to provide
His authority over the Roman army
questions.explain: Moved with compassion for the crowd, Jesus miraculously multiplies a small amount of food to feed thousands.

questions.q: When Jesus calmed the storm on the lake, the amazed disciples asked what kind of man he was. What does this miracle reveal about him?
options: His ability to forecast the weather
questions.explain: By stilling the wind and waves with a word, Jesus shows divine authority over the natural world.

questions.q: How did Jesus enter Jerusalem in the days before his death?
questions.explain: Jesus rode a donkey into Jerusalem as crowds shouted 'Hosanna', fulfilling prophecy of a humble king.

questions.q: For how much did Judas Iscariot agree to betray Jesus?
questions.explain: Matthew records that the chief priests paid Judas thirty pieces of silver to betray Jesus.

questions.q: At the Last Supper Jesus shared bread and wine, saying 'This is my body' and 'This is my blood'. What did this signify?
options: His coming sacrificial death for others
The end of the Passover festival
questions.explain: The bread and wine pointed to Jesus' body and blood given up in his sacrificial death on the cross.

questions.q: Jesus predicted that Peter would deny knowing him. How many times did Peter deny Jesus before the cock crowed?
questions.explain: Just as Jesus foretold, Peter denied him three times before the cock crowed, then wept bitterly.

questions.q: Which Roman governor questioned Jesus and released Barabbas to the crowd?
questions.explain: Pontius Pilate presided over Jesus' trial and released the prisoner Barabbas at the crowd's demand.

questions.q: Matthew records that at the moment Jesus died, the curtain of the temple was torn in two. What is this most often understood to symbolise?
options: New access to God opened through Jesus' death
questions.explain: The torn temple curtain is widely interpreted as the barrier between God and people being removed by Jesus' death.
